state.misconception_label: Ignores negative sign when expanding bracket

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: John is expanding these three brackets: \( (x+5)(x-3)(x+6) \) He finds it helpful to split the first bracket and view the problem as follows: \( x(x-3)(x+6)+5(x-3)(x+6) \) He expands the brackets further. Before he simplifies, what are the terms than contain an \( \boldsymbol{x}^{2} \) ? I got \( \begin{array}{l}+6 x^{2} \\ +3 x^{2} \\ +5 x^{2}\end{array} \) because I forgot that two negatives multiply to a positive.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let me ask you this: what would happen if you tried your method on a simpler version of the problem?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Okay, I guess I could try it with something simpler, like \( (x+2)(x-1) \). If I split it like before, I’d have \( x(x-1) + 2(x-1) \). But I’m still not sure how to keep track of the negative sign when I expand it. Can you help me with that part?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let me ask you this: what would happen if you focused on the signs when expanding the brackets in the simpler version of the problem you just mentioned?
